note: REVIEW PROPOSAL — not applied. D1 is canonical; disk lags. Apply approved changes via the Worker API (POST /api/article/:slug with base_version), keyed by (slug, annotation id). Suggestions are human-gated: a unique last-segment match is a hint, not a proof.

annotations.label: Two points determine a line
annotations.note: Mathlib has `affineSpan` of two points but no single canonical statement equivalent to Euclid's `two points determine a line` axiom.

annotations.label: Cartesian closed categories correspond to typed λ-calculus
annotations.note: Mathlib defines Cartesian closed categories but does not formalize the equivalence with simply typed λ-calculus.

annotations.label: Division ring is semisimple
annotations.note: Instance making a division ring semisimple is present in `SimpleModule.Basic`.

annotations.label: Euclidean geometry
annotations.note: Mathlib has the `EuclideanGeometry` namespace built on inner product / affine spaces, which is a model of Euclidean geometry but not the axiomatic 'satisfies all of Euclid's axioms' definition.

annotations.label: Fermat's Last Theorem for regular primes
annotations.note: Kummer's proof of FLT for regular primes is not in core Mathlib; the FltRegular project (built on Mathlib) has formalized the Case I result.

annotations.label: Functional equation for L-functions
annotations.note: Mathlib has functional equations for Riemann zeta and Dirichlet/Hurwitz L-functions (e.g. in `Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/RiemannZeta.lean`, `AbstractFuncEq.lean`), but not the general Langlands L-function functional equation.

annotations.label: Triple product zero iff linearly dependent
annotations.note: Combining `triple_product_eq_det` with determinant-linear-dependence characterizations gives the result, but it is not stated explicitly for the triple product.

annotations.label: Complex representation and modular group action
annotations.note: SL(2,ℤ) and its action on the upper half-plane are formalized, but no statement identifies its orbits with equivalence classes of 2D lattices.

annotations.label: Tannaka–Krein duality
annotations.note: Mathlib has a Tannaka-style reconstruction for module categories (`ModuleCat.Tannaka`); full Tannaka–Krein duality for compact groups is not present.

annotations.label: Topology on series in several variables
annotations.note: Product/pi topology on `MvPowerSeries σ R`.

annotations.label: Norm is multiplicative
annotations.note: The `NormedDivisionRing ℍ` instance bundles `norm_mul a b = ‖a‖ * ‖b‖`; `normSq` is also a `MonoidWithZeroHom`.

annotations.label: Poisson summation formula
annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes classical Poisson summation `∑ f(n) = ∑ 𝓕(f)(n)` under Schwartz-like hypotheses on `f`.

annotations.label: Proper subset
annotations.note: Proper subset `⊂` on `Set α` is provided through the `HasSSubset` instance (`a ⊂ b ↔ a ⊆ b ∧ ¬ b ⊆ a`) available on any preorder including `Set α`.

annotations.label: Superset
annotations.note: `⊇` is the flip of `⊆` on `Set α`, available via the `HasSubset`/`LE` instances defined in Mathlib.Data.Set.Defs (read directly).

annotations.label: Bimodule
annotations.note: Bimodules have no dedicated class but are expressed as `[Module R M] [Module Sᵐᵒᵖ M] [SMulCommClass R Sᵐᵒᵖ M]`, as documented in this file.

annotations.label: Surreal numbers form a Field
annotations.note: `Surreal` is defined in Mathlib with a `LinearOrderedCommGroup`/field-like structure; being a proper class it is not a `Field` in the type-theoretic sense but the surreal number arithmetic satisfies the field axioms.

annotations.label: Lattice arrangement
annotations.note: Mathlib defines `ZLattice` (a discrete cocompact ℤ-submodule of a real vector space) which underlies lattice packings, but does not formalize lattice packings themselves.

annotations.label: FOIL method for binomial multiplication
annotations.note: FOIL `(a+b)(c+d) = ac+ad+bc+bd` is an immediate consequence of `mul_add`/`add_mul`; not bundled as a separate named lemma but routinely closed by `ring`.

annotations.label: Two points define a line
annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes the affine line through two points and its minimality in affine geometry, but not for hyperbolic lines.

annotations.label: Three or more terms in proportion; geometric progressions (Def. 8)
annotations.note: Geometric progressions exist in Mathlib (e.g., `geom_series`, `geom_sum_eq`), but Euclid's Definition 8 itself is not formalized.

annotations.label: Homological algebra
annotations.note: Chain complexes and homology are formalized in `Mathlib.Algebra.Homology`; the discipline as a whole is not a single object.

annotations.label: Projective planes exist for prime power orders
annotations.note: Mathlib supplies a `ProjectivePlane` instance for ℙ K (Fin 3 → K), giving prime-power-order planes via finite fields, but no general existence statement.

annotations.label: Riemannian manifold
annotations.note: Mathlib has `ContMDiffRiemannianMetric` and `IsContMDiffRiemannianBundle` for Riemannian metrics on the tangent bundle, but no top-level `RiemannianManifold` structure.

annotations.label: Solutions of the ODE satisfy the integral equation
annotations.note: Mathlib's `picard_eq_of_hasDerivAt` proves exactly this implication: if α has the right derivative on [t₀, t], then `picard f t₀ (α t₀) α t = α t` (i.e. α equals its own Picard image). The converse is `hasDerivWithinAt_picard_Icc`, and `IsP

annotations.label: Artin–Wedderburn theorem (Wedderburn's part)
annotations.note: `isSemisimpleRing_iff_pi_matrix_divisionRing` (and `exists_ringEquiv_matrix_divisionRing` for simple Artinian rings) is the Artin–Wedderburn structure theorem.

annotations.label: Rational root theorem
annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes the rational root theorem via `num_dvd_of_is_root` and `den_dvd_of_is_root`: for a polynomial with integer coefficients, the numerator of any rational root divides the constant term and the denominator divides the leading

annotations.label: Equality of ordered pairs
annotations.note: Prod.mk.injEq: `((a,b) = (c,d)) = (a = c ∧ b = d)` (verified via loogle).

annotations.label: Proper subset
annotations.note: Proper subset `⊂` on `Set α` is provided via the `HasSSubset` instance derived from the partial order.

annotations.label: Focal subgroup theorem
annotations.note: `commutator_inf_eq_focalSubgroup` in `Mathlib.GroupTheory.Focal` is the Focal Subgroup Theorem: `commutator G ⊓ P = P.focalSubgroup`.

annotations.label: Eisenstein series as automorphic form
annotations.note: `eisensteinSeriesMF` packages the weight-k Eisenstein series as a `ModularForm` for congruence subgroups.

annotations.label: Minkowski's theorem
annotations.note: This file states the Minkowski Convex Body Theorem in both strict and compact-domain forms.

annotations.label: Liouville's transcendence criterion
annotations.note: Mathlib's `exists_pos_real_of_irrational_root` produces the Liouville inequality `1 ≤ (b+1)^d * |α − a/(b+1)| * A` underlying the criterion.

annotations.label: Gram–Schmidt process
annotations.note: `gramSchmidt 𝕜 f` produces the orthogonal sequence from a linearly independent one; `gramSchmidtNormed` gives the orthonormal version.

annotations.label: Orthogonal projection onto a subspace
annotations.note: `Submodule.orthogonalProjectionOnto K` (with legacy alias `orthogonalProjection`) is the continuous linear projection of a Hilbert space onto a complete subspace `K`.

annotations.label: Projection construction of representing vector
annotations.note: Mathlib has orthogonal projections and the Riesz map, but I did not find the article's projection formula for the representing vector as a named theorem.

annotations.label: Norm as distance to affine hyperplane
annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes nearest-point projection machinery, but I did not find this dual-norm-as-distance-to-hyperplane formula.

annotations.label: Projection minimum point of hyperplane
annotations.note: `starProjection_minimal` proves the metric minimality of orthogonal projection, but not the exact affine-hyperplane statement from the article.

annotations.label: Unit vector construction of representing vector
annotations.note: Mathlib has unit-vector projection formulas, but I did not find this Riesz representing-vector construction as a named theorem.

annotations.label: Stone space is compact; isolated types
annotations.note: The CompactSpace instance on CompleteType T α is proved (the isolated-points correspondence is not separately formalized).

annotations.label: Field of fractions of K[[X]] equals K((X))
annotations.note: `instance {K : Field} : IsFractionRing K⟦X⟧ K⸨X⸩` in `LaurentSeries.lean`.

annotations.label: Gaussian elimination for linear systems
annotations.note: Mathlib formalizes Gaussian-elimination-style reductions via transvection decompositions and row echelon reductions on matrices.

annotations.label: Exponentiation
annotations.note: Monoid.npow (with HPow notation ^) defines raising a base to a natural-number power.

annotations.label: Exponentiation (positive integer exponent)
annotations.note: `Monoid.npow` is the canonical inductive definition of iterated multiplication on a monoid.

annotations.label: Inductive definition of positive integer exponentiation
annotations.note: `Monoid.npow_zero` and `Monoid.npow_succ` provide the inductive base and step.

annotations.label: Exponentiation in a monoid
annotations.note: `Monoid.npow` is monoid exponentiation.

annotations.label: Matrix power
annotations.note: Square matrices form a monoid, so `A^n` is given by `Monoid.npow`; many `Matrix.*_pow` lemmas exist.

annotations.label: Nonnegative integer powers
annotations.note: `Monoid.npow` (exposed via `HPow`/`^`) defines nonnegative integer powers with `npow_zero` and `npow_succ`.

annotations.label: Nonnegative integer powers
annotations.note: `Monoid.npow`/`HPow` provide ℕ-indexed powers in a monoid/ring.

annotations.label: Peano axiom 5 (induction)
annotations.note: Nat.rec is the core induction/recursion principle for ℕ.

annotations.label: Mathematical induction
annotations.note: The principle of mathematical induction on ℕ is built into Lean as Nat.rec; Mathlib's Nat.le_induction in Mathlib.Data.Nat.Init packages the usual 'base + step' form.

annotations.label: Principle of mathematical induction
annotations.note: The induction principle for ℕ is the core recursor `Nat.rec`, available throughout Mathlib.

annotations.label: Proofs by mathematical induction
annotations.note: Mathematical induction is the recursor Nat.rec, generated automatically with the natural numbers (Lean core).

annotations.label: Nimbers form a Field
annotations.note: `Nimber` carries a `Field` instance (`Nimber.instField`) in `Mathlib/SetTheory/Nimber/Field.lean` via nim-addition and nim-multiplication.

annotations.label: Set exponentiation
annotations.note: `E^F` is represented by the function type `F → E` in Lean.

annotations.label: Quotient by irreducible polynomial is algebraic extension
annotations.note: Mathlib proves the quotient by the span of a polynomial has finrank equal to its natDegree, with field structure for irreducible polynomials via `AdjoinRoot.instField`.

annotations.label: Discrete ↔ compact under Pontryagin
annotations.note: Mathlib has instances making `PontryaginDual` discrete when the source is compact (and vice versa).

annotations.label: Unit quaternion and versor
annotations.note: Unit quaternions are not a named subgroup, but can be expressed via `unitary ℍ` or `Metric.sphere (0:ℍ) 1`; no dedicated `UnitQuaternion`/`versor` declaration exists.

annotations.label: Distance between quaternions
annotations.note: Distance `dist a b = ‖a - b‖` follows from the `NormedAddCommGroup ℍ` instance.

annotations.label: Quaternions form a metric space
annotations.note: `NormedAddCommGroup ℍ` (plus `CompleteSpace ℍ`) endows quaternions with a metric/complete metric space structure.

annotations.label: Norm scales by absolute value of real scalar
annotations.note: The `NormedAlgebra ℝ ℍ` instance (and `Quaternion.norm_coe`) makes scalar multiplication norm-multiplicative: `‖r • q‖ = |r| * ‖q‖`.

annotations.label: Reduction of ratios
annotations.note: Rational numbers are stored in reduced form via `Rat`, but ratio-reduction as a named operation is not a separate Mathlib concept.

annotations.label: Higher Tor functors and derived tensor product
annotations.note: Mathlib defines `Tor n : C ⥤ C ⥤ C` in `CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Tor`; a single packaged 'derived tensor product' term is not standard.

annotations.label: Adjoint is transpose under Riesz identification
annotations.note: Mathlib proves the defining inner-product identity for adjoints, but I did not find a named theorem identifying adjoint with transpose under Riesz equivalence.

annotations.label: Adjoint-transpose equality
annotations.note: The adjoint's inner-product characterization is available, but the exact adjoint-transpose equality through Riesz maps was not found as a declaration.

annotations.label: Average over a sphere
annotations.note: Circle (2D sphere) average is formalized; the higher-dimensional sphere-average operator specific to harmonic analysis is not.

annotations.label: LTI filter output via convolution
annotations.note: Mathlib defines `convolution` and many properties, but does not package the LTI-system/impulse-response equation as a distinguished result.

annotations.label: Convolution of input and system
annotations.note: Mathlib defines `convolution f g L` in `Mathlib.Analysis.Convolution` for functions on an additive group, generalizing the signal-processing convolution.

annotations.label: k-th exterior power of the cotangent space
annotations.note: Mathlib has `exteriorPower` on general modules, but not applied to a manifold cotangent space (which does not exist as a type).

annotations.label: Compatibility with scalar product
annotations.note: `mul_smul` is the action axiom `(a * b) • x = a • b • x`.

annotations.label: Polar reciprocation / dual polytope
annotations.note: The polar set of a subset (`polar`) is defined in Mathlib but not specialised to polytopes.

annotations.label: Conjugate of a product reverses order
annotations.note: Inherited from `StarRing ℍ[R,c₁,c₂,c₃]`: `star (a * b) = star b * star a`.
